html:
The joining of the British Northern and Southern Nigeria protectorates into one colony on 1 January 1914, under the governor Frederick Lugard.

The name Nigeria had been coined by the journalist Flora Shaw in 1897. The north, the former Sokoto Caliphate, was ruled through its emirs under indirect rule, with few mission schools; the south, with ports, missions and cash crops, changed faster. The two halves were run very differently for decades. That gap, and the rivalry of the Hausa-Fula, Yoruba and Igbo regions, shaped the politics of independent Nigeria and the civil war.
sum: The joining of the British Northern and Southern Nigeria protectorates into one colony on 1 January 1914, under the governor Frederick Lugard.
